origin: Original workshop built by Muse (AI assistant) on 20 November 2026 at Steven Powell's direction, from the wave-2 candidate list in the Everyday Cool ideas side chat that morning: he picked Sound and Time from the list and set the order himself ('start with sound and time'), then expanded Sound twice in his own words — music and music theory belong in it because 'music is basically math geometry with sound' (with a cross-link to Everyday Math both ways), and the little piano bench was his design: a small piano / virtual MIDI keyboard that lets you pick an instrument and play notes, with links to MIDI archives and the ability to load a MIDI file into the keyboard or compose one. The room carries a tone bench (frequency, nearest note, wavelength, with the small-speaker honesty line), a decibel ladder with the +10 dB = ×10 intensity math and the NIOSH 85 dB / 3 dB hearing-safety criteria, a strings & skins bench, echo ranging with the thunder rule, sound-speed comparisons across air, water, and steel, and the bone-conduction card for why a recorded voice sounds strange. Its music wing carries intervals as frequency ratios with the equal-temperament honesty line (the tempered fifth is 1.498, not the pure 3:2), rhythm as fractions that must sum to a measure, and the circle of fifths drawn as geometry. The little piano plays two octaves in five synthesized voices (piano, organ, plucked string, bell, synth — stand-ins, not recordings, and the page says so), by mouse, touch, computer keys, or a Web MIDI keyboard where the browser allows; it loads Standard MIDI Files and plays them on the keys, ships a public-domain Ode to Joy demo, and records what you play into a downloadable .mid written by its own round-trip-tested SMF writer, all locally in the browser. The banner shows a friendly robot with one hand cupped to its ear, sound waves drawn as teal-and-gold ribbons carrying notes, a guitar and a drum on the bench. It enters the catalog under 'Science,' immediately after Everyday Physics, as the eleventh door of The STEM Room. This folder is the maintained original.
